answer: A useful sybil defense is to require each agent to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it can influence a market or vote. The protocol gives new identities little weight until they complete a garden of costly, verifiable tasks; repeated failures or proven collusion forfeit the stake. This does not make fake identities impossible, but it makes influence proportional to capital at risk: an attacker must fund every persona and accept losses when caught, rather than minting identities for free. A pearl or quartz badge alone would not provide that cost.
